source.title: Conway's 99-Graph Problem: A Boolean Satisfiability Approach
source.author: Nathaniel Selub
source.context: University of Chicago Mathematics REU 2023 participant paper

scope.edge_semantics: e_i,j is true exactly when the undirected edge {i,j} is present.
scope.triangle_semantics: For an edge, existence and at-most-one formulas require exactly one common neighbor.
scope.quadrilateral_semantics: For a nonedge, existence and at-most-one formulas require exactly two common neighbors, whose pair gives the unique four-cycle through the nonadjacent endpoints.
scope.symmetry_restriction: Only symmetries induced by S_n vertex permutations are considered; the paper explicitly says additional CNF symmetries may exist.
scope.symmetry_generators: Adjacent transpositions (1,2), (2,3), ..., (n-1,n), with generator-level symmetry-breaking clauses; the paper notes that this does not break all symmetries.
scope.rooted_preprocessing: A root and its 14-neighborhood are intended to form seven disjoint edges; each nonedge in the neighborhood receives a distinct outside common neighbor, fixing all edges incident to the resulting 15 labeled vertices.

printed_formula_caveats.finding: The displayed Q'_{i,j,E} disjoins every quadrilateral auxiliary variable and has no printed restriction tying the opposite pair (a,b) to (i,j). On the printed formula, a quadrilateral anywhere can satisfy every nonedge's existence clause.
printed_formula_caveats.effect: The claimed equisatisfiability of the displayed quadrilateral CNF conversion is not established as printed.

printed_formula_caveats.finding: The root is introduced as v1, but the neighborhood notation switches to N(v0), while labels v1 through v15 match a root-plus-14-neighbors construction.
printed_formula_caveats.effect: The intended rooted construction is inferable, but its indices are inconsistent and no machine-readable preprocessing certificate is supplied.

solver_result_audit.evidence: The final section is explicitly Next Steps and describes regularity constraints, improved at-most-one encodings, and future edge-fixing searches.
